question: The alpine biome is usually located at altitudes above ________ and extends to the area just below the snow line.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3000 m.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The alpine biome is usually located at altitudes above 3000 m and extends to the area just below the snow line.**
 
• Tundra biome is further classified into the Arctic and Alpine. 
 
• Alpine Tundra occurs at high mountains like the Himalayas, Andes, Alps, etc.
 
• This region is devoid of trees due to permafrost. 
 
• The lowest form of vegetation like mosses and lichens are found in this region. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 **There are two different types of Tundras:-**

 
• Alpine Tundra:

 
 
• Alpine Tundra occurs in mountains where trees can't grow at high altitudes.
 
• The growing season is about 180 Days.
 
• Habitants found in these areas are:
 
 
• Mountain Goats,
 
• Sheep, Marmots,
 
• Birds feed on low-lying plants, and
 
• Insects.
 
 
 
 
 
• Arctic Tundra:
 
 
• ​Arctic Tundra extends from the edge of the arctic ocean down to the coniferous forest of the Taiga. 
 
• Permafrost (which contains 14% of the Earth's Carbon) prevents trees from taking root but Shrubs and
 
• Other vegetation grows during the short summers which range 50-60 days.
 
• A variety of wildlife found in the Arctic areas are:
 
 
• Polar Bears,
 
• Arctic foxes, and
 
• Caribou.
